slides.text: I'm an air traffic controller. We handle stress, weather delays, and emergencies daily. But Flight 404 broke every protocol. The Boeing 737 vanished from radar over the Atlantic in 2012. No distress signal, no wreckage. Just gone. Twelve years later, on a quiet Tuesday night shift, a blip appeared on my screen. The transponder code matched exactly. Flight 404 was descending toward runway three. The radio crackled with heavy, terrifying static.

'Tower, this is 404 requesting immediate landing,' a voice gasped. It was Captain Miller. I knew his voice from the archived tapes. He sounded completely terrified. I cleared the runway, my hands shaking as the massive jet touched down silently in the thick fog. Emergency crews surrounded it. The engines died. I watched from the tower as the breach team forced the cabin door open. My radio flared to life with the rescue commander's voice.

'Tower... you need to see this,' the commander stammered, his voice laced with pure dread. 'The plane is completely empty. No passengers, no luggage. But the coffee in the cockpit is still piping hot.' Suddenly, my private control room door clicked, locking itself. A cold hand clamped over my mouth from behind, and a familiar voice whispered in my ear. 'Good job clearing the runway. Now, it's time for us to board the next flight.'
